options.configuration: Local browser customers; Universal Login database passkeys; password fallback; MFA/stronger-step-up unverified

conditions: Select local browser customers on an Auth0 Database Connection with Universal Login passkeys. Do not inherit brokered workforce, native/mobile, M2M, trial, paid or custom-database capabilities.

Free pricing includes passkeys but excludes Pro MFA factors. Generic MFA factors are subscription-dependent: https://auth0.com/docs/secure/multi-factor-authentication/multi-factor-authentication-factors. Neither guide verifies configurable MFA entitlement for this B2B Free scope.

Passkey inclusion and a biometric/PIN prompt do not alone verify the project's multifactor capability, independent-factor properties or effective tenant policy. Keep MFA UNKNOWN, not provider-wide UNAVAILABLE; no paid upgrade is proposed.
The Free offer is not an observed account entitlement, quota or future zero-cost guarantee. No tenant, subscription, account, credential, enrollment, provider call or policy mutation occurred.

evidence.summary: Free pricing includes passkeys and excludes Pro MFA factors. Documented passkeys do not verify configurable MFA entitlement, factor properties or policy for this customer scope; MFA remains UNKNOWN.

conditions: Availability is a conditional mechanism-level inference from domain-bound WebAuthn passkeys: https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/database-connections/passkeys. Bind the intended HTTPS RP/domain and validate authenticator behavior; this is not all MFA or every login.

Universal Login, Identifier First and compatible database identifiers are prerequisites; disable Classic custom login pages. Custom database without import is Early Access and outside this scope. No deployed settings or tenant entitlement were verified.

Passkey-enabled database connections must still have passwords enabled. Organization invitation signup initially uses a password; progressive enrollment can be delayed. A passkey toggle or login button does not establish compulsory phishing-resistant authentication.

Enrollment, password reset, recovery, credential removal, existing SSO and administrator paths require independent bypass review. Journey enforcement remains UNKNOWN. Seven earlier Auth0 scopes, AuthWeave's ZITADEL/BFF and synthetic evaluator are unchanged.

evidence.summary: The configuration guide documents passkey prerequisites, required password fallback and invitation/enrollment exceptions. Mechanism availability is conditional; complete customer-journey enforcement remains UNKNOWN.

conditions: The database passkey guide explicitly describes syncing credentials across devices. A passkey, local biometric/PIN, platform attachment or successful WebAuthn login does not prove a hardware-bound, non-exportable private key.

Hardware-only enrollment, trusted attestation and enforceable key-protection policy are not verified. Synced, cross-device, existing credential and recovery paths need separate review; keep both fields UNKNOWN, not provider-wide UNSUPPORTED.

Do not inherit subscription-dependent WebAuthn MFA security-key examples as Free entitlement or infer NIST AAL. No hardware purchase, physical-device test, enrollment, attestation validation or custom login implementation occurred. Residency and other clients/populations remain omitted.

evidence.summary: The passkey guide explicitly allows credential synchronization across devices. It does not establish hardware-only/non-exportable key availability or enforcement for the selected Free customer journey.

conditions: The web step-up guide documents Actions requesting MFA and application validation of the ID-token amr claim. MFA configuration is a prerequisite; this generic guide does not verify Free-plan factor entitlement. Stronger-factor availability therefore remains UNKNOWN.

The example uses an MFA acr_values request, api.multifactor.enable('any') and allowRememberBrowser. Those examples do not prove a selected stronger factor, passkey-only challenge, fresh authentication or an essential-ACR higher-assurance contract.

Validate signed token issuer/audience/expiry and request binding before trusting claims; independently verify required factor and freshness at the sensitive-operation gate. Absent or insufficient evidence must deny. Step-up means stronger authentication, not repeating the same login.

The guide warns amr can be absent after silent authentication or refresh. Cached SSO, token refresh, an mfa label or a remember-browser bypass is not evidence of fresh stronger authentication. No Action, protected operation, token or bypass test was executed; enforcement stays UNKNOWN.

evidence.summary: The generic web step-up guide documents MFA Actions, validated amr checks and silent/refresh limitations. Free entitlement, selected stronger factors, freshness and operation gating are unverified; both fields remain UNKNOWN.
